meta.title: Requirements
meta.description: Browsers, React and TypeScript versions, frameworks and server rendering, bundle size and the accessibility target of React Scheduler.

browsers.intro: The package targets current browsers and is tested in three engines on every change.
rows: The last two, and the current ESR
browsers.features: Four platform features are used without a fallback, because every browser in that matrix has them:
points: <dialog> with showModal(), for the overflow and detail dialogs.
ResizeObserver and IntersectionObserver, for compact mode and for pinning.
Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.PluralRules, for every date, time and count.
CSS logical properties and :where(), which is what makes right-to-left work without a second stylesheet.

react.intro: React 18.2, 18.3 and 19.x. CI runs the whole test suite against each of them, so a release cannot pass while one of them is broken.
react.strict: Strict Mode is supported: every effect the component starts is idempotent and cleans up after itself, so a double-invoked effect changes nothing.

typescript.intro: TypeScript 5.0 or newer. The declarations are generated from the source and shipped with the package; they are checked against TypeScript 5.0, 5.9 and 7.0. Anything older cannot resolve the package's subpath exports.
typescript.generics: The types are generic over your own data: the item type, the level keys and the tag keys all flow through, so renderItemDetail receives your item and not a widened one. See Model types.

frameworks.intro: Any React application. The package is published as ESM and CommonJS, with types for both, and it never touches the DOM while rendering.
points: Vite, React Router and every bundler that reads the exports map.
<link to="/integrations/nextjs/">Next.js</link>, App Router and Pages Router: the schedule is a client component.
<link to="/integrations/ssr/">Server rendering</link> in general: the first render is the server's markup, and the observers start after hydration.
Node 22 or newer, if you render on a server.

size.intro: Measured by size-limit on every change, minified and gzipped, with React excluded. A build that grows past a budget fails.

a11y.intro: The target is WCAG 2.2 level AA.
a11y.tested: Automated checks run axe with the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA rules in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and no serious or critical violation is allowed. The release checklist adds a manual pass with NVDA in Firefox and VoiceOver in Safari: headings, list counts, card announcements and dialog focus. What is not covered yet is listed under <link to="/discover-more/accessibility/">Accessibility</link>.
